source_title: AI Act Omnibus: first political trilogue ends without agreement
summary: The first political trilogue on the Digital Omnibus on AI ended without agreement on 29 April 2026 after about 12 hours of negotiations. The sticking point was the conformity-assessment architecture for AI in regulated products under Annex I: Parliament pushed to move sectoral legislation (machinery, medical devices, toys) from Section A to Section B, letting sectoral safety law handle those AI systems; the Council resisted, to preserve AI Act oversight for sensitive sectors. A follow-up trilogue is scheduled for about 13 May 2026. The Cypriot Council Presidency must close the file before its term ends 30 June 2026; otherwise the Lithuanian Presidency takes over from 1 July. If the Omnibus is not formally adopted before 2 August 2026, the original AI Act obligations (Regulation 2024/1689, Article 113) apply as written on that date. Multiple advisory firms (IAPP, DLA Piper, Modulos) now recommend preparing against the original 2 August 2026 deadline rather than the proposed extensions.
mechanical_change: No change to the AI Act text. The proposed delay (2 Dec 2027 for standalone Annex III, 2 Aug 2028 for Annex I products) remains a proposal, not law. Original deadlines remain legally binding.
verified_by: IAPP, Modulos, The Next Web, Computerworld, Ropes & Gray — multiple independent legal and policy sources confirmed the trilogue outcome
